blocks.text: From the module B1.3 Readings are without vowels, such as newspapers, websites and messages. An Arabic reader does not see the vowels, he reconstructs them: the same spelling ⁧علم⁩ may be ⁧عِلْم⁩ • science • ⁧عَلَم⁩ The flag of the country concerned shall be the flag of the Union. ⁧عَلِمَ⁩ • came to know, or ⁧عَلَّمَ⁩ The reader chooses in a fraction of a second thanks to grammar and context. In this unit make this choice aware: learn the five most frequent types of ambiguity (active or passive, verb or name, simple or derived form, verb person, prefix or root), the grammatical spies that resolve them and a strategy in five steps. You also start the timed reading: at the end of B1 you will have to read short news in silence at least 70 words per minute, with a summary. Three weeks.

blocks.text: How do you decide? After the article or a preposition there is a name: ⁧فِي العِلْمِ⁩ , ⁧بِالعَمَلِ⁩ . A word followed by a name to the name that may be its subject at the beginning of the sentence is probably a verb: ⁧عَمِلَ أَبِي فِي مِصْرَ⁩ . A word that holds a genitive (iḍāfa) is a name: ⁧عَمَلُ أَبِي⁩ It's my father's work. And the meaning decides the last choice: ⁧عَلَمُ البَلَدِ⁩ The flag of the country is not the science of the country.
